problems.quote: Remember that rotation is invertible only when s and L are coprime
problems.problem: A cyclic rotation (shift) on a block of length L is always invertible for any shift s (1 ≤ s < L); the inverse is rotation by L−s. The condition that s and L are coprime is required for the permutation to be a single cycle, not for invertibility.
problems.correction: Remember that rotation forms a single cycle only when s and L are coprime
problems.verifierReason: Original confuses invertibility (always true for rotations) with single-cycle property (requires coprime). Correction is accurate.

problems.problem: 99 has digit sum 18, not 9; no two-digit multiple of 11 has digit sum 9, so the intersection is empty
problems.correction: Together they have no common value, so the combination is insufficient

problems.quote: knowing only the radius and an inscribed angle does not determine the chord length unless the central angle is also known
problems.problem: An inscribed angle determines the central angle (central angle = 2 × inscribed angle), so radius and inscribed angle together do determine chord length
problems.correction: knowing only the radius and an inscribed angle determines the chord length via the central angle
problems.verifierReason: Inscribed angle determines central angle (2×), allowing chord length from radius. Correction is correct.

problems.quote: A clue such as 'A sits third to the left of B' is interpreted differently depending on whether A faces the centre
problems.problem: In circular seating puzzles, 'to the left of B' is always from B's perspective, so the facing direction that determines left/right is B's, not A's.
problems.correction: A clue such as 'A sits third to the left of B' is interpreted differently depending on whether B faces the centre
problems.verifierReason: Left/right in seating puzzles is always from the reference person's (B's) perspective, not the subject's (A's).
